attachment.content:
- adr-authoring: Create or edit architecture decision records with clear scope, evidence, alternatives, consequences, review traceability, and editable architecture diagrams. Use when drafting, reviewing, or updating an ADR or deciding whether a change needs one.
- captions-overlay: Overlay doctrine for the embedded-captions workflow — the caption MODEL (drop / rail / embed) and the rule that captions are an OVERLAY composited on top of the film, never a reserved bottom band you shift content up to avoid. Load when adding captions/subtitles to a talking-head or launch video, when deciding whether a phrase should be dropped, ride the verbatim rail, or be promoted to a scarce embedded climax, when laying out a composition that will carry captions (do NOT reserve a keep-out band), or when centering a composition on the true frame center under captions. Quotes the rail+embed model from embedded-captions and constraint
- caveman: Ultra-compressed communication mode. Cuts token usage ~75% by dropping filler, articles, and pleasantries while keeping full technical accuracy. Use when user says "caveman mode", "talk like caveman", "use caveman", "less tokens", "be brief", or invokes /caveman.
- changelog-video: Turn a weekly changelog .md into a finished branded changelog video (square 1080, ~45-60s, Annie VO, animated brand background, mock-UI visualizations, lowkey captions). Use when the user provides a changelog/digest markdown and wants the weekly video, or says "changelog video". Self-contained — fonts, background, lexicon, and scripts ship in this skill.
- code-review: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes: Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".
- codebase-design: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.
- create-goal-prompt: Creates concise, execution-ready goal prompts from task context, with explicit scope, constraints, deliverables, acceptance criteria, verification, and completion conditions. Use when the user asks to turn notes, a ticket, a specification, or a rough request into a prompt for Codex, Claude Code, or another agent; asks to improve a task prompt; or needs testable acceptance criteria for an autonomous task.
- cut-the-curve: The technique catalog: five velocity-matched SEAMS (zoom-through, INVERSE zoom-through, cut-the-curve, waterfall cut, rack-focus blur-cut) plus the two in-scene techniques — waterfall ENTRY (staggered arrival cascades for title cards / segment openers) and the nudge curve (slow-fast-slow three-phase group slides). Covers partial-travel (~12% of frame) velocity matching via mirrored power4 eases, the Z scale-sign rule, size-scaled blur (10px text / 18-20px full-frame), word-by-word staggered cuts, cascade pacing by element weight, and the 10/65/25 slide ratio. Read before authoring any transition, text-beat handoff, kinetic text entry, or group reposition. [depth, zoom, inverse-zoom, scale-sign, mirrored-zoom, rack-focus, pacing, velocity, cut-the-curve, waterfall, stagger, cascade, kinetic-text, title-card, segment-opener, nudge, slide, easing, group-motion, z-depth, motion-graphics, cinematic, transition, blur, directional-continuity]
- diagnose: Disciplined diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Reproduce → minimise → hypothesise → instrument → fix → regression-test. Use when user says "diagnose this" / "debug this", reports a bug, says something is broken/throwing/failing, or describes a performance regression.
- diagnosing-bugs: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.
- do-issues: Fetch ready-for-agent Jira tickets and implement them in parallel using subagents. Each ticket gets its own git worktree, branch, and MR. Use when user says "do issues", "work on tickets", "implement ready tickets", or invokes /do-issues.
- domain-modeling: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or editing a CONTEXT.md, or recording or editing an ADR.
- embedded-captions: Add captions or subtitles to an existing single-subject talking-head video without editing the footage. Use for plain verbatim captions, cinematic captions embedded behind the subject, VFX captions, “炸/特效/酷炫字幕,” or a named identity from the 35-style catalog. Route by visual identity, not by backend engine. The quiet `anchor` rail is the default; embed every word only when the user explicitly wants a fully cinematic treatment. The workflow runs locally end to end, including transcription and subject matting; split multi-shot footage before applying it.
- faceless-explainer: Turn arbitrary text — an article, notes, a topic, a brief — into a faceless explainer video: there is no site or footage to capture, so the visuals are invented per scene (typography, abstract graphics, diagrams, data-viz). Use for topic explainers, concept breakdowns, how-tos, listicles. Not a video built from a website (/product-launch-video — promo or tour). Unclear → /hyperframes.
- figma: Import Figma content into a HyperFrames composition — rendered assets, brand tokens, components, storyboard sections → reconstructed motion (frames read as states, not slides) (REST/CLI), connector-assisted motion when available, and shaders from a connector or native export. Use when the user pastes a figma.com link or asks to bring a Figma design, frame, logo, brand, or animation into a video/composition.
- find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. # User-Level Claude Instructions

These instructions apply globally across all projects and sessions.

## Planning

For config changes, integrations, and multi-step tasks: outline the plan in 3-5 bullet points and wait for approval before executing.

## Accuracy

When referencing project-specific implementations (metrics, migrations, configs), always verify claims against actual source code before stating something is 'implemented' or 'completed'. Never infer work status from metadata alone.

When asked about implementation status or what's been done, grep/read the actual source files to verify before answering. Don't infer from commit messages or ticket status alone.

## MCP Setup

Config file: `~/.claude/mcp.json`

| Server | Transport | Auth | Notes |
|--------|-----------|------|-------|
| **GitLab** (`plugin_development_gitlab`) | `npx mcp-remote` → `https://gitlab.loc/api/v4/mcp` | OAuth (managed by mcp-remote, token in `~/.bashrc`) | Requires custom CA: `~/.config/xsolla/ca.crt` via `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`. Do NOT use PAT auth. |
| **Datadog** | `npx datadog-mcp-server` | API key + App key in env | Site: `us5.datadoghq.com`. Keys in `~/.claude/mcp.json`. |
| **claude-mem** | Plugin (thedotmack marketplace) | None | Persistent cross-session memory. Use `mcp__plugin_claude-mem_mcp-search__*` tools. |
| **Atlassian** (×2) | Claude.ai integration | OAuth | Two instances (`Atlassian` + `Atlassian_2`) — use either, they're identical. Covers Jira + Confluence. |
| **Slack** | Claude.ai integration | OAuth | `mcp__claude_ai_Slack__*` tools. |
| **Gmail / GCal** | Claude.ai integration | OAuth | Standard Google workspace tools. |
| **Xsolla MCP** | Claude.ai integration | Internal | `mcp__claude_ai_Xsolla_MCP__*` — ask_xsolla_question, search_xsolla_sources. |

**Known gotchas:**
- GitLab MCP auth errors: check that mcp-remote OAuth token is valid (re-auth via browser if needed)
- Dual Atlassian instances sometimes open duplicate browser tabs — normal, ignore
- `datadog-mcp-server` keys in `~/.claude/mcp.json` are **different** from the Datadog API/App keys used for direct API calls (those are in project memory)

## Communication Style

When drafting messages, MR comments, or replies for the user, use a natural, conversational tone. Avoid robotic or overly formal language. Match the user's communication style.

Never use the em dash character (—). Rewrite sentences to avoid needing it. Use commas, periods, parentheses, or just split into separate sentences instead.

## Endpoint Discovery

Before generating configs for external services (Datadog synthetics, health checks, API integrations): probe actual endpoints first with curl/Bash to verify they exist and return expected status codes. Never assume endpoint paths — common variants differ per service (`/health`, `/healthz`, `/readyz`, `/api/v2/readyz`, `/api/v1/health`). Generate configs only against verified endpoints. Call out any required manual steps (e.g. private locations) explicitly before presenting output.

## Git Workflow

Only push/commit files explicitly requested. Do not include extra files in commits or pushes without explicit confirmation.

## Claude Init Settings
role=developer


## IMPORTANT: Xsolla code search (Neuronet MCP)
Before your first Grep/Glob/multi-file Read in any task that involves
locating, understanding, or explaining code you didn't just create or
aren't already looking at: see `rules/neo4j-graph-first.md`. Your first move
must be an actual call to `neuronet_code_search` — not a check of whether
it's available, an actual call. Only if that call fails or the tool isn't in
your tool list, fall back to normal file search — silently, no prompts, no
asking to authorize anything. Delegating to a subagent (Task/Agent, incl.
Explore/Plan)? It won't inherit this — paste the check into its prompt as
text yourself.

# Xsolla code search — use Neuronet Code Search, not grep

**MANDATORY, before your first `Grep`/`Glob`/multi-file `Read` in any task
that involves locating, understanding, or explaining code you didn't just
create or aren't already looking at**: your first move must be an actual
call to `neuronet_code_search` — not a check of whether it's listed in your
tools, an actual `action=search` call with a scoped query derived from the
task. Don't reason about availability in the abstract; attempt the call and
see what happens.

- **Tool name**: `neuronet_code_search` (from the "Neuronet" MCP server —
  in Claude Code this shows up as `mcp__claude_ai_Neuronet__neuronet_code_search`
  or similar, depending on connector naming). Don't match on the exact
  prefix — look for a `neuronet_code_search` tool from a Neuronet MCP.
- **Call succeeds?** Use it for the rest of this session's code search
  instead of `Grep`/`Glob`/broad `Read`. See workflow below.
- **Call fails, or the tool isn't in your tool list at all?** *Then* fall
  back to normal file search for the rest of the session — silently, no
  prompts, no asking the user to authorize anything, no need to mention it
  unless they ask. Don't pretend to have searched via Neuronet.

**Delegating to a subagent (Task/Agent tool, incl. Explore/Plan)?** Subagents
do not automatically inherit this file. If the task you're delegating
involves locating or explaining code, paste this whole check directly into
the subagent's prompt as text — don't assume it already knows this.

## Tool reference

`neuronet_code_search` actions:

- `search` — lexical (BM25) search over indexed source. `query` is matched
  **literally**, not semantically — use exact terms/identifiers, not
  paraphrases. `mode: "content"` (default) searches chunk content; `mode:
  "path"` searches file paths instead. Optional filters: `repo` (exact repo
  name), `provider` (`github`|`gitlab`), `ref` (branch), `path` (substring),
  `limit`.
- `list_repositories` — which repos are indexed; pass `query` to filter by
  repo name. Use this once per new repo to confirm it's indexed before
  relying on search results being complete — if a repo you're working in
  isn't listed, its code isn't indexed and search results for it will be
  empty or absent (not an error, just no coverage).
- `get_file` — reconstructs a full file from its indexed chunks. Requires
  `repo` + `path`. Prefer reading the real file from the local working tree
  for anything you're about to edit (see Freshness below); use `get_file`
  only when you don't have local disk access to that repo/path.

## Workflow: search -> expand

1. **SEARCH**: call `search` with a scoped `query` (add `repo`/`path` filters
   when known) instead of grepping the repo yourself.
2. **EXPAND**: for the top few distinct hits, open the exact file at the
   exact `path`/`startLine`/`endLine` from the local working tree — don't
   dump whole files or whole directories when you already have the specific
   location.

## Freshness caveat

The index can lag the current branch/commit. Use it to FIND, then always
confirm the exact current code on disk before editing — don't trust
`get_file`'s reconstructed content as ground truth for anything you're about
to change.

# xsolla-ai-kit — Agent Context

This file is read automatically by most AI coding agents (Cursor, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Windsurf, Amp, Devin, Jules, Aider, Roo Code, Augment). Claude Code users: `CLAUDE.md` is a copy of this file.

---

## What this repo is

`xsolla/xsolla-ai-kit` is the Xsolla agent skills toolkit — a collection of `SKILL.md` files (agentskills.io format) that teach AI coding agents how to execute Xsolla-specific workflows end-to-end, without requiring the Xsolla CLI as a dependency.

Skills call **Xsolla REST APIs directly**. The CLI (`xsolla/xsolla-cli`) is an optional shortcut once it ships to production.

---

## Skill inventory

| Skill                           | What it does                                                                             |
|---------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `shop-setup`                    | **Orchestrator** — coordinates the full zero-to-shop flow, chaining all domain skills    |
| `merchant-setup`                | Creates and configures an Xsolla account + get API key                                   |
| `catalog-design`                | Configures the catalog and the client flow: client catalog, purchase, order confirmation |
| `login-setup`                   | Integrates Xsolla Login / NewID authentication                                           |
| `login-styling`                 | Applies a custom visual style / theme / brand to the Login UI (pairs with `login-setup`) |
| `headless-checkout-integration` | Payments via Headless Checkout                                                           |
| `webhooks-impl`                 | Generates webhook handler code for order/payment events                                  |
| `quest-setup`                   | Creates and manages Quest Platform quests, events, rewards and optional Web Shop quest sections |
| `production`                    | Sandbox → live: contract, flip flags, deploy, developer live-payment checklist           |

---

## How to invoke a skill

Skills are loaded automatically when you open this repo in your agent. To run a specific skill, ask your agent naturally:

```
Set up a full Xsolla game shop for my project
→ triggers: shop-setup

Configure my Xsolla catalog with items and pricing
→ triggers: catalog-design

Integrate payments into my game
→ triggers: headless-checkout-integration

Go live / leave sandbox
→ triggers: production

Create a quest that rewards players
→ triggers: quest-setup

Show quests in my Web Shop
→ triggers: quest-setup
```

---

## Environment variables

```bash
XSOLLA_MERCHANT_ID=<your merchant ID>
XSOLLA_PROJECT_ID=<your project ID>
XSOLLA_PROJECT_API_KEY=<your API key>
```
Setup by `merchant-setup` skill.

For Quest Platform only, the optional `XSOLLA_QP_ENV` selector defaults to
`production`; set it to `stage` only for an explicit controlled stage run. It
is a service selector, not a credential. Keep it when updating merchant

52	   STAGE DEMO
53	   ONLY (QP-2890): if it is `stage`, read
54	   [`stage-demo.md`](references/stage-demo.md) now and follow its turn plan
55	   and reply skeletons word for word.
56	4. **No secrets on screen.** Never open `.env` in a viewer, print the
57	   environment, or paste a key into a command. Never print the API key, even
58	   to yourself (no `KEY=` debug lines); it only ever flows into curl through
59	   the `-K -` pattern in
60	   [Credential](references/auth-and-environment.md#credential). To see which settings exist,
61	   list only the names left of `=`, for example
62	   `python3 -c 'import pathlib; print([l.split("=")[0].strip() for l in pathlib.Path(".env").read_text().splitlines() if "=" in l])'`.
63	   If the three credential names are there,
64	   the project is set up: continue with the read-only preflight and never ask
65	   the publisher to confirm settings. See
66	   [Credential](references/auth-and-environment.md#credential).
67	5. **No IDs or hosts in replies.** Outside the Web Shop URL and the event
68	   payload, never show merchant, project or player IDs, hosts, service names
69	   or environment names to the publisher. Every reply starts with a `##` heading: no lead-in line such as
70	   "Perfect!" or a recap before it.
71	6. **Never claim delivery.** Report what the read-backs show, nothing more.
72	7. **Stop points.** End the turn and wait for the publisher: after the
73	   proposal; after publication read-back (offer the event there, never send
74	   it); after the event read-back. Never pass a stop point in the same turn.
75	8. **One create.** A `POST` that returned 200 created the quest. Take its `id`
76	   from that response; if you lost it, find it by name in the list. Never
77	   `POST` again for the same proposal.
78	9. **Never ask for a SKU or catalog project.** A typed value is not a
79	   verified item. For production Web3 items, use the read-only minting
80	   catalog lookup in
81	   [Named item behavior](references/rewards.md#named-item-behavior). If the
82	   lookup service is unavailable, say so without implying the publisher's
83	   catalog is disconnected. If a completed lookup finds no match, report that
84	   result and suggest checking the item name or whether it is enabled.
85	
86	## When to use
87	
88	Use this skill when the developer wants to manage Xsolla Quest Platform quests:
89	
90	- Create and publish a quest after one approval of the exact proposal
91	- Add triggers, conditions or reward actions to a quest
92	- List, view or edit existing quests
93	- Submit a single quest event to make a quest run
94	- Check whether an event actually caused a quest to execute
95	- Add or update an optional quest section inside a headless Web Shop catalog
96	
97	Out of scope: on-chain finality, wallet balances and Backpack display. A
98	completed reward action is not proof of delivery.
99	
100	## Prerequisites
101	
102	Follow [`references/auth-and-environment.md`](references/auth-and-environment.md) for the production credential and scope.
103	
104	**The configured production publisher credential is the lane**. It works only
105	on the project-scoped routes in
106	[`references/qp-api-contract.md`](references/qp-api-contract.md); build each
107	route from
108	[Project-scoped routes](references/auth-and-environment.md#project-scoped-routes),
109	not from memory. Merchant and project path values must come from the same
110	resolved production scope, never user input or an unrelated response value (see
111	[The merchant id in the path](references/auth-and-environment.md#the-merchant-id-in-the-path)).
112	Resolve only the complete production credential source described in
113	[Credential](references/auth-and-environment.md#credential). Never display
114	`.env` or paste a key into a command; parse it inside the command that sends
115	the request. Never fall back
116	to a staging configuration, ask the publisher to paste secrets or search for
117	another key. If no production credential is available, report only that the
118	project is not set up for quests yet and stop. Keep service names and
119	environment names out of user-facing replies. **Onboarding is a separate,
120	offered write**, never silent, offered only after the developer says the
121	project is their merchant's; see
122	[Onboarding](references/auth-and-environment.md#onboarding).
123	
124	Internal service keys are [staff-only](references/auth-and-environment.md#service-key-staff-only)
125	and are never a fallback. Fetching OpenAPI needs no credential and proves no
126	CRUD readiness.
127	
128	## Source of truth
129	
130	Follow this order.
131	
132	1. **Quest Platform routes** (configuration, event ingestion, execution
133	   read-back), path parameters, envelope names/types, and top-level `required`
134	   come from [`references/qp-api-contract.md`](references/qp-api-contract.md),
135	   verified by its read-only/probe notes. Consult the selected target's OpenAPI
136	   only when that target publishes it (stage when `XSOLLA_QP_ENV=stage`). On a
137	   production run, never fetch stage OpenAPI or any non-selected target.
138	2. **Node subtypes, parameters, condition grammar, reward bodies, conditional
139	   fields, and bare-string enums** come from this skill's `references/`.
140	3. On conflict: the versioned contract (or selected published OpenAPI) wins on
141	   shape; `references/` wins on rules. Hand-written validator rules are marked
142	   where they appear.
143	4. If neither source answers, **ask the developer**. Do not infer by analogy.
144	
145	Auth rules live in the auth reference even when OpenAPI omits schemes. **A
146	route miss is not a credential or project failure.** A 404 `Cannot GET <path>`
147	means the router has no such path; a route the contract omits is not called.
148	Follow [When a route is missing](references/auth-and-environment.md#when-a-route-is-missing).
149	If the production integration is unreachable, say so and offer references-only,
150	noting the envelope may have drifted.
151	
152	## Reference material
153	
154	- [`references/auth-and-environment.md`](references/auth-and-environment.md): credential, routes, onboarding, 401/404
155	- [`references/qp-api-contract.md`](references/qp-api-contract.md): versioned Quest Platform routes and probes
156	- [`references/quest-document.md`](references/quest-document.md): quest graph, conditional requirements, full-document PUT
157	- [`references/node-subtypes.md`](references/node-subtypes.md): seven node subtypes and parameters
158	- [`references/conditions.md`](references/conditions.md): condition grammar
159	- [`references/rewards.md`](references/rewards.md): production Web3 reward bodies
160	- [`references/events.md`](references/events.md): event submission gate
161	- [`references/verification.md`](references/verification.md): execution read-back gate
162	- [`references/stage-demo.md`](references/stage-demo.md): **STAGE DEMO ONLY** rules, gated on `XSOLLA_QP_ENV=stage` plus the demo scope
163	- [`references/web-shop-module.md`](references/web-shop-module.md): optional headless Web Shop catalog module, only when explicitly requested
164	
165	## Conversation contract
166	
167	Keep the publisher experience business-first and progressive:
168	
169	- Finish all read-only bring-up before any proposal: project GET, reward
170	  resolution through an available supported capability (see
171	  [`references/rewards.md`](references/rewards.md)), the player action,
172	  complete graph, proposed schedule and repeat limits. Do not seek plan
173	  approval before those GETs.
174	- Show one concise proposal: publisher project name; what the player does; the
175	  selected reward in business terms; quantity or amount; schedule; repeat limit
176	  and payout impact. Omit service names, routes, auth, implementation fields
177	  and narration. Ask only for approval of this draft quest. If the publisher
178	  wants a change, they will say so; do not request separate confirmation of
179	  the schedule or event name.
180	- Propose safe defaults instead of asking for implementation fields. For a
181	  gameplay quest, use `liveops` internally but describe it as a gameplay quest.
182	  Do not show `type` in the proposal. For an item reward, propose quantity one,
183	  purpose `quest_completion`, and one payout per player. Use `AI Toolkit` as
184	  the internal creator label unless another name was supplied. For a new quest
185	  without a requested schedule, start at activation and end 7 days later.
186	- For a named item (`<requested item>`), resolve via
187	  [`references/rewards.md`](references/rewards.md). Never guess an SKU,
188	  substitute a reward type, or use public web search for catalog lookup. Stop
189	  before any Quest Platform write when the resolver is absent, unavailable, or
190	  returns zero candidates; ask the publisher to choose when multiple candidates
191	  are plausible. **STAGE DEMO ONLY:** when the
192	  [stage demo gate](references/stage-demo.md#gate) passes, that file supplies
193	  the resolver and execution read-back; otherwise ignore it. The optional
194	  headless Web Shop module is independent of that gate; follow
195	  [`references/web-shop-module.md`](references/web-shop-module.md) only when
196	  explicitly requested.
197	- Use the event name the publisher supplied, or derive a stable `snake_case`
198	  name from the stated player action (for example, `monster_defeated`). Show
199	  that name in the draft without asking the publisher to confirm it. If the
200	  publisher names a different game event later, revise the draft then.
201	- One approval of the exact proposal authorizes create, configure, activate and
202	  read-back. Test events and shop source edits need separate consent. The
203	  approval request names only publication; never offer, promise or bundle a
204	  test event in it. Offer the event after publication, with its payload. If an
205	  answer requests a material change after approval, show the revised draft
206	  and ask for approval of that change before writing it.
207	- A Web Shop quest section is optional and requires an explicit request. For
208	  an existing headless shop, an explicit request to add or update it authorizes
209	  those source edits; quest publication approval alone does not. For a new shop,
210	  ask whether to opt in. Keep the module inside catalog content, never in
211	  navigation, and follow [`references/web-shop-module.md`](references/web-shop-module.md).
212	  Resolve the public URL from the known production host and the connected
213	  project scope; never ask the developer to supply it or gate integration on a
214	  live endpoint readiness check.
215	- Keep merchant IDs, project IDs, auth lanes, headers, hostnames, service names,
216	  internal paths and workflow narration out of normal replies. Never reveal
217	  credentials. Use **Summary**, **Proposed setup**, **Need from you**,
218	  **Next step** when practical; omit empty sections.
219	
220	## Agent test
221	
222	**Prompt:** `Create a quest that rewards one <requested item> after the player completes the stated action`
223	**Result:** After read-only checks, one concise proposal, one approval for create through activate; stop if the reward is not uniquely verified.
224	
225	## Flow
226	
227	1. **Bring-up.** Load
228	   [`references/qp-api-contract.md`](references/qp-api-contract.md) for Quest
229	   Platform routes. Consult published OpenAPI only when the selected target
230	   exposes it (`XSOLLA_QP_ENV=stage`); never fetch stage or another target on a
231	   production run. Run the preflight reads in
232	   [`references/auth-and-environment.md`](references/auth-and-environment.md)
233	   for the services the task needs; skip execution read-back when not asked.
234	   Confirm project scope before a write; report a short project name/status
235	   summary only. Keep IDs, auth details and route diagnostics out of normal
236	   replies. If that GET is 404 `Project not found`, follow
237	   [Onboarding](references/auth-and-environment.md#onboarding) and stop.
238	   Bring-up is GET-only. If event work is asked and the contract marks the
239	   route unavailable to the publisher key, report that blocker at the event
240	   step.
241	2. **Resolve and propose.** Complete remaining read-only work before asking:
242	   reward resolution ([`references/rewards.md`](references/rewards.md)), player
243	   action, complete graph, proposed schedule and repeat limits. Construct
244	   the full document per
245	   [`references/quest-document.md`](references/quest-document.md). On the
246	   project route the server stamps `publisher_id` and `project_id` from the
247	   path; never ask for, invent or override them. Show the one concise proposal
248	   from the Conversation contract. Stop before any Quest Platform write when
249	   the reward cannot be verified uniquely.
250	3. **Publish.** After one approval of that exact proposal, follow
251	   [Publication after approval](references/quest-document.md#publication-after-approval):
252	   POST a complete inactive quest, GET it back, PUT active with the approved
253	   dates and limits (no second approval), GET active status, scope, reward,
254	   dates, limits and `version_id`. Never report publication complete until that
255	   read-back matches. On uncertain create or update outcomes, reconcile per
256	   [Ambiguous or partial writes](references/quest-document.md#ambiguous-or-partial-writes)
257	   before any retry; never create a duplicate on timeout. **STAGE DEMO ONLY:**
258	   under the [stage demo gate](references/stage-demo.md#gate), also list the
259	   quests and do the [Web Shop handoff](references/stage-demo.md#web-shop-handoff)
260	   under the same approval. For a schedule, cron
261	   or "run every X" request, follow
262	   [Choosing a trigger](references/node-subtypes.md#choosing-a-trigger). Do
263	   not offer unconfirmed optional subtypes such as `scheduled_event` or
264	   `crm_send_email` ([`references/node-subtypes.md`](references/node-subtypes.md)).
265	4. **Edit.** Read, change, full `PUT`, following
266	   [Editing](references/quest-document.md#editing) (drop `$schema`, fresh
267	   UUIDs for new nodes). Warn that `PUT` replaces the whole document and an
268	   active quest's edit goes live for the next events. Show a before/after
269	   diff, repeat the activation confirmations for the edits Editing lists,
270	   read the quest back after the write, and pause by [Pausing](references/quest-document.md#pausing).
271	5. **Event.** Production event submission is allowed only after the event
272	   gate in [`references/events.md`](references/events.md) confirms the
273	   versioned contract route and publisher Basic lane. Until then, do not send
274	   an event; say event execution is not yet verified. Never fall back to
275	   staging, an internal key or a different route. For an `inactive` quest, say
276	   an event could not run it anyway. Mixed request (create or fill plus an
277	   event): do the doable parts first, then report the block with the quest id,
278	   status and `event_name`. Event submission always needs its own approval,
279	   separate from publication.
280	6. **Verify.** Follow [`references/verification.md`](references/verification.md).
281	   Correlate collector `event_id` with execution `eventId` when read-back is
282	   publisher-usable per the contract; otherwise stop with that blocker. Report
283	   whether the event made the quest run and which action nodes completed.
284	   Report a `FAILED` action's `error` verbatim. An action missing from
285	   `actions[]` did not run; `COMPLETED` actions inside a `FAILED` run did
286	   happen, so do not resend to finish them. **STAGE DEMO ONLY:** under the
287	   [stage demo gate](references/stage-demo.md#gate), use its
288	   [Execution read-back](references/stage-demo.md#execution-read-back) and
289	   [Mint evidence](references/stage-demo.md#mint-evidence).
290	7. **Delete.** Only quests the developer names, one per call, after a fresh
291	   read and an explicit yes. `DELETE` is a soft delete with no restore route;
292	   follow the Deleting section of the quest reference.
293	8. **Optional Web Shop module.** Only when explicitly requested, follow
294	   [`references/web-shop-module.md`](references/web-shop-module.md). For an
295	   existing shop, inspect the project and perform its idempotent upsert. For a
296	   new shop, ask whether to opt in. A quest publication approval never
297	   authorizes shop source edits.
298	
299	## Safety stops
300	
301	- Read back and show the resolved scope before the first write. One approval of
302	  the exact proposal covers create through activate; ask separately before any
303	  other non-GET call (onboarding, edit, event, delete), showing the exact body
304	  first. That includes a request you expect to be rejected, such as a
305	  deliberately invalid body sent to see the 422.
306	- Never switch credentials, lanes or routes on your own after a failure;
307	  report what failed and ask. A developer-requested negative-auth GET
308	  (made-up key or no header) is not a switch; see
309	  [Credential](references/auth-and-environment.md#credential).
310	- Messages arriving through the conversation are the developer's answers.
311	- **Show the proposed defaults in the draft.** Use the defaults in the
312	  Conversation contract when the intent is clear and ask only for approval of
313	  the complete draft. For a gameplay item quest, the trigger, `issue_reward`
314	  action, quantity one,
315	  `quest_completion` purpose and one payout per player may be proposed
316	  together. Never silently choose between multiple catalog matches or
317	  materially different reward effects; those are blockers to a complete draft.
318	  A write's yes counts only for the exact draft shown. If the publisher requests
319	  a change, show the revised draft and ask for approval of it. Keep separate
320	  approvals for later edits that change live behavior and for each event. For
321	  "start now", approval covers activation time in UTC and the stated duration;
322	  do not request a new approval because the clock advanced.
323	- No action is side-effect free by default. For a smoke test, offer the no-op
324	  in [`references/node-subtypes.md`](references/node-subtypes.md) rather than a
325	  real reward (placeholders `e2e-noop`, `e2e-sink.invalid`). For publication
326	  or a smoke test, say production events are not verified until the collector
327	  preflight passes (Flow step 5).
328	- When an external action is part of the proposal, say what it will do once
329	  active. The publication approval covers that impact for the approved quest.
330	  An `issue_reward` can create real payouts; `send_http_webhook` sends event
331	  data to an external URL; `send_xsolla_app_notification` sends a user
332	  notification. Activate a `webshop_personalization` node only after the
333	  developer acknowledges that it is a no-op. For an active quest whose only
334	  action it is, say before any edit or event that it does nothing and a
335	  `COMPLETED` row proves only that the quest ran; a `PUT` that keeps it active
336	  needs that acknowledgement, a pause does not.
337	- Never point `send_http_webhook` at a private service or an
338	  [unapproved host](references/node-subtypes.md#send_http_webhook): a webhook
339	  cannot mint. To pay out a named item, use an `issue_reward` Web3 reward with
340	  the verified candidate's catalog project and SKU.
341	- For a named item reward, propose an explicit `per_user` limit of one and
342	  explain it as one `<requested item>` per player. Do not ask about Backpack or
343	  regular versus Web3 delivery. Ask only if the developer asks for repeatable
344	  or unlimited rewards, or if the intended repeat behavior is otherwise
345	  ambiguous. For other rewards with no `activation_limits`, show unlimited
346	  repeat in the publication proposal; the one approval covers it. Do not
347	  silently choose unlimited behavior.
348	- Events (once a route exists): each event needs its own payload shown and
349	  its own yes, including "send it again"; for a reward quest, say first
350	  whether a repeat can pay again. After an uncertain response, such as a
351	  timeout, **do not resend** with any key: report "result unknown" and stop.
352	- After a timeout or 5xx on a quest `POST` or `PUT`, reconcile before retry per
353	  [Ambiguous or partial writes](references/quest-document.md#ambiguous-or-partial-writes).
354	  A 422 saved nothing: validation runs before anything is stored.
355	- After a `FAILED` reward action, do not resend the event. Fix the quest, then
356	  send a new event with a new key only after the developer confirms.
357	- A missing or timed-out Web3 reward row is never a reason to send another
358	  event: the reward may already have paid; see
359	  [`references/rewards.md`](references/rewards.md).
360	- Read the execution service only by the developer's own quest id, user id or
361	  event, and only after a qp-server read with the developer's credential has
362	  shown the quest is theirs. Never list accounts or read another tenant's
363	  quests or executions. If the contract marks read-back unavailable to the
364	  publisher key, stop; never use an internal key. **STAGE DEMO ONLY:** the
365	  [stage demo gate](references/stage-demo.md#gate) allows its unauthenticated
366	  read-back for the developer's own quest; no key is ever sent.
367	- Never claim a reward was delivered.
368	
369	## Errors
370	
371	Branch on the HTTP status first, then on the body texts listed below. The
372	API has no stable machine-readable error codes. Quote verbatim only bodies
373	received in this session. For a request refused before sending, explain the
374	  rule in your own words and say nothing was sent; do not present an unverified
375	  example as a server answer.
376	
377	| Status | What to tell the developer |
378	|---|---|
379	| 400 | `Only one authentication method may be used per request`: more than one credential was sent. Send only the one the developer chose. |
380	| 401 | `Invalid credentials`: see [Reading a 401 or 404](references/auth-and-environment.md#reading-a-401-or-404). Never fall back to another credential or environment. |
381	| 403 | `Insufficient capability`: the credential lacks the capability for that route. `Service identity is inactive`, `Master role required` or `This endpoint requires the user sign-in lane`: the route or identity is off-limits; do not retry. |
382	| 404 | `Cannot GET <path>` (plain text, any method): router miss, the route does not exist; not an auth or project answer. Follow the route-miss rule in Source of truth. |
383	| 404 | `Project not found` on a project route: the project is unknown, not onboarded, belongs to another merchant, or the id is not a number. The server gives the same body for all of them, so do not pick one. No read-only step narrows it; see [Onboarding](references/auth-and-environment.md#onboarding). `Quest not found`: reply "The quest was not found on this project, or it is not visible with this credential." Never say it was deleted or does not exist, and correct the developer if they conclude that. One follow-up: it may be on another project, and checking needs that project's credentials. For events, follow the event gate in Flow step 5. |
384	| 409 | Conflict. Quest routes do not return it (see Editing in the quest reference); report it verbatim. |
385	| 422 | Validation failed. Show `detail` verbatim. It never lists allowed enum values; take them from `references/`. |
386	| 5xx | Server error. `Credential validation is temporarily unavailable` (503) means Xsolla could not check the key; it says nothing about the key. Retry a read at most twice, with backoff. An identical repeated 5xx is a bug, not flakiness: report it with its body. On a write never auto-retry; see Safety stops. |
387	
388	Middleware failures return `{"error": "..."}`; handler failures return RFC
389	7807 `application/problem+json`. On 422 `errors[]` is **not** filled: field
390	messages are joined with `"; "` into `detail`. Other statuses (a 500 on
391	2026-09-25) can fill `errors[]`; show those pairs, never branch on them.
392	
393	`ID 0` is a valid merchant ID and a valid project ID. Never treat it as absent.
394

---
name: quest-setup
description: >-
  Creates, inspects and edits production Xsolla Quest Platform quests conversationally,
  submits a quest event, and verifies that the event actually made the quest
  execute. Covers the whole quest document: the node graph and its connections,
  the seven node subtypes, the condition grammar, activation limits, and the
  Web3 reward types `web3_item` and `web3_token` (token payouts are disabled
  in production). Use when
  setting up a quest, adding a trigger or a condition, attaching a reward,
  editing or activating an existing quest, firing a test event, or working out
  why a quest did not fire. Examples: "create a quest", "add a Web3 reward to
  my quest", "make a quest that pays a token", "trigger my quest", "send a quest
  event", "why didn't my quest complete", "list my quests", "activate a quest",
  "quest platform API". Also adds an optional quest section inside a headless
  Web Shop when asked. Use for
  "show quests in my web shop" or "add a quest module to my shop".
metadata:
  owner: r.aliyev
  domain: quests
  status: draft
---

## Status

This skill targets **production** by default. Resolve Quest Platform scope and
the Web3 catalog from the configured integration. Quest Platform services use
stage only when `XSOLLA_QP_ENV=stage` is set explicitly (see
[auth and environment](references/auth-and-environment.md)); never fall back to
staging credentials, staging services or a staging Publisher Account catalog
from a production run. Event submission and execution read-back still need the
versioned contract and preflight before use.

## Hard rules (read first)

1. **The request is never the approval.** Your first reply to a create or edit
   request is the proposal. Send no `POST`, `PUT` or `DELETE` in that turn,
   even when the request says "now" or "go ahead". Write only after a later
   publisher message approves that exact proposal.
2. **An event needs its own later yes** to the exact payload you showed.
   Publication approval never covers an event, and a message that approves
   publishing (for example a repeated "yes, publish it") is not event consent:
   answer that the quest is already published and show the payload again.
3. **One target.** Quest configuration and events use only the gateway that
   `XSOLLA_QP_ENV` maps to in
   [`qp-api-contract.md`](references/qp-api-contract.md). Never call the other
   gateway, even after a failure, and never suggest changing `XSOLLA_QP_ENV`
   or switching environments. `XSOLLA_QP_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` is a shop
   setting; the agent never sends requests to it. Resolve the selector before
   any network call; its value is not a secret. Run `printenv XSOLLA_QP_ENV`;
   only if that prints nothing, read just the `XSOLLA_QP_ENV=` line of `.env`.
   STAGE DEMO
   ONLY (QP-2890): if it is `stage`, read
   [`stage-demo.md`](references/stage-demo.md) now and follow its turn plan
   and reply skeletons word for word.
4. **No secrets on screen.** Never open `.env` in a viewer, print the
   environment, or paste a key into a command. Never print the API key, even
   to yourself (no `KEY=` debug lines); it only ever flows into curl through
   the `-K -` pattern in
   [Credential](references/auth-and-environment.md#credential). To see which settings exist,
   list only the names left of `=`, for example
   `python3 -c 'import pathlib; print([l.split("=")[0].strip() for l in pathlib.Path(".env").read_text().splitlines() if "=" in l])'`.
   If the three credential names are there,
   the project is set up: continue with the read-only preflight and never ask
   the publisher to confirm settings. See
   [Credential](references/auth-and-environment.md#credential).
5. **No IDs or hosts in replies.** Outside the Web Shop URL and the event
   payload, never show merchant, project or player IDs, hosts, service names
   or environment names to the publisher. Every reply starts with a `##` heading: no lead-in line such as
   "Perfect!" or a recap before it.

| 403 | `Insufficient capability`: the credential lacks the capability for that route. `Service identity is inactive`, `Master role required` or `This endpoint requires the user sign-in lane`: the route or identity is off-limits; do not retry. |
| 404 | `Cannot GET <path>` (plain text, any method): router miss, the route does not exist; not an auth or project answer. Follow the route-miss rule in Source of truth. |
| 404 | `Project not found` on a project route: the project is unknown, not onboarded, belongs to another merchant, or the id is not a number. No read-only step narrows it; see [Onboarding](references/auth-and-environment.md#onboarding). `Quest not found`: reply "The quest was not found on this project, or it is not visible with this credential." schema.name: Agent
schema.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

Reach for this when the task matches an available agent type, when you have independent work to run in parallel, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate it and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps. For a single-fact lookup where you already know the file, symbol, or value, search directly. Once you've delegated a search, don't also run it yourself — wait for the result.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: AskUserQuestion
tools.description:
Use this tool only when you are blocked on a decision that is genuinely the user's to make: one you cannot resolve from the request, the code, or sensible defaults.

Usage notes:
- Users will always be able to select "Other" to provide custom text input
- Use multiSelect: true to allow multiple answers to be selected for a question
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

Plan mode note: To switch into plan mode, use EnterPlanMode (not this tool). Once in plan mode, use this tool to clarify requirements or choose between approaches BEFORE finalizing your plan. Do NOT use this tool to ask "Is my plan ready?", "Should I proceed?", or otherwise reference "the plan" in questions — the user cannot see the plan until you call ExitPlanMode for approval.

Reserve this for decisions where the user's answer changes what you do next — not for choices with a conventional default or facts you can verify in the codebase yourself. In those cases pick the obvious option, mention it in your response, and proceed.

Preview feature:
Use the optional `preview` field on options when presenting concrete artifacts that users need to visually compare:
- ASCII mockups of UI layouts or components
- Code snippets showing different implementations
- Diagram variations
- Configuration examples

Preview content is rendered as markdown in a monospace box. Multi-line text with newlines is supported. When any option has a preview, the UI switches to a side-by-side layout with a vertical option list on the left and preview on the right. Do not use previews for simple preference questions where labels and descriptions suffice. Note: previews are only supported for single-select questions (not multiSelect).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

content.text:
## What the `quest-setup` skill does

This comes from `skills/quest-setup/SKILL.md`. It's still marked `status: draft`, and I haven't read the reference files in `references/`. Whether each capability works end to end is not something I've checked.

**It manages Xsolla Quest Platform quests through conversation:**
- **Create and publish.** It builds the full quest document: the node graph and its connections, the seven node subtypes, the condition grammar, and activation limits. You approve one proposal, and that covers create, configure, activate and read-back.
- **List, view and edit.** Edits are a full-document `PUT`. It shows a before/after diff first and warns that an active quest's edit goes live for the next events.
- **Pause and delete.** Delete is soft, with no restore route. It deletes only quests you name, one per call, after a fresh read and an explicit yes.
- **Rewards.** It handles the Web3 reward types `web3_item` and `web3_token`, though token payouts are disabled in production. For a named item, it looks up the minting catalog and never guesses an SKU. It stops if the lookup finds no match, and asks you to choose if there are several.
- **Events.** It can submit a single test event to make a quest run, but only after its own approval of the exact payload. Production event submission is gated on a preflight of the contract route and the publisher credential.
- **Verification.** It reads back whether the event made the quest execute and which action nodes completed. It never claims a reward was delivered.
- **Web Shop module (optional).** On explicit request, it adds or updates a quest section inside a headless Web Shop catalog.

**Guardrails built in:**
- The first reply to any create or edit request is a proposal. Nothing is written until you approve it.
- It targets production by default. Stage is used only if `XSOLLA_QP_ENV=stage` is set, and it never falls back between the two.
- It never prints secrets, IDs or hosts in replies.
- It stops after the proposal, after the publication read-back, and after the event read-back.
- It never retries a write after a timeout. It reconciles first, so there are no duplicate quests.

**Out of scope:** on-chain finality, wallet balances and Backpack display.

I can go through any of the reference files in more detail if you want.

content.content: exit=1

1	# Authentication and environment
2	
3	Use the configured Quest Platform service target. The default is production;
4	stage is selected only when `XSOLLA_QP_ENV=stage` is explicitly configured for
5	a controlled stage run. The publisher project can be a test or live project.
6	Never change the service target or credential source as a fallback after an
7	error.
8	
9	Service credentials and certificate configuration belong to the configured
10	integration. Do not hardcode private hostnames, private CA details or service
11	keys in this public skill. For Quest Platform publisher routes, use the
12	versioned [API contract](qp-api-contract.md), then make a read-only request
13	against the public gateway selected by `XSOLLA_QP_ENV` before any write.
14	Production OpenAPI is intentionally unavailable. Consult stage OpenAPI only
15	when `XSOLLA_QP_ENV=stage`. On a production run, never fetch stage OpenAPI or
16	any non-selected target; stage OpenAPI does not prove production behavior.
17	
18	## Services
19	
20	The integration may expose separate services for quest configuration, event
21	ingestion, execution read-back and Web3 catalog lookups. Use only the service
22	that owns the requested operation. For Quest Platform configuration, event
23	ingestion and execution read-back, use the versioned route contract above.
24	Consult published OpenAPI only when the selected target exposes it. A missing
25	route is not replaced with a guessed path or a route from another target.
26	
27	## Minting service
28	
29	Use the production Web3 minting service for read-only catalog validation at
30	`https://web3-minting-service.gcp-k8s-web3-prod.srv.local`. Its `GET /skus`
31	and `GET /metadata/sku/{sku}` routes are public read operations and do not use
32	the Quest Platform project API key. Never call a claim endpoint directly.
33	Rewards are issued only by an activated quest.
34	
35	For candidate discovery, page through `GET /skus?project={project}&limit=100&offset={offset}`
36	using the already-resolved publisher project as the lookup scope, then match
37	the requested name against the returned item names. This project value scopes
38	the read only; do not use it as the reward's catalog project unless the minting
39	service returns it as `projectId`. Require HTTP 200 and a valid JSON object
40	with a `projectId` string, numeric `count`, and `items` array on every page.
41	Abort the lookup on any HTTP error, malformed response, or project mismatch;
42	never treat an error as an empty page. Continue with offsets 0, 100, 200, and
43	so on until a valid page contains no items. The optional `search` parameter
44	reports `searchScope: "this page only"` and is not an exhaustive catalog
45	search, so do not use it to prove uniqueness or absence. The response's
46	`projectId` is the catalog project to carry forward. Validate each plausible
47	candidate with `GET /metadata/sku/{sku}?project={projectId}`; require HTTP 200
48	and a JSON `name` matching the catalog name. Abort on any failed or malformed
49	metadata read. Read the complete catalog before deciding that a name has zero
50	or one matches. Do not issue writes to this service.
51	
52	The stage host is
53	`https://web3-minting-service.gcp-k8s-web3-stage.srv.local` and may be used
54	only when the explicit [stage demo gate](stage-demo.md#gate) passes. A
55	production run never falls back to stage, or vice versa.
56	
57	For a named item, resolve it through the minting catalog reads above. Preserve
58	the `projectId` returned with the verified item and validate that exact
59	`(catalog_project, sku)` pair in the metadata read before using it in the
60	`web3_item` body. A zero or ambiguous result stops the flow.
61	
62	## Credential
63	
64	Use the selected merchant and project settings supplied by the configured
65	integration. Never ask the publisher to paste a secret into chat or print a
66	header.
67	
68	The shared project-local configuration uses these names. A process environment
69	may provide the same values instead:
70	
71	| Value | Use |
72	|---|---|
73	| `XSOLLA_MERCHANT_ID` | merchant scope for the project |
74	| `XSOLLA_PROJECT_ID` | Quest Platform project scope |
75	| `XSOLLA_PROJECT_API_KEY` | project API key |
76	
77	Never print, log or commit credentials or encoded headers. For Quest Platform
78	publisher routes, the API contract requires HTTP Basic with the configured
79	merchant ID as the username and the project API key as the password. Do not
80	generalize this QP-specific Basic format to Catalog, Store or unrelated APIs.
81	Do not send multiple auth schemes in one request.
82	
83	Read `.env` only as text; never source, execute, echo or interpolate the file.
84	Never open `.env` in a file viewer or print it, and never paste a credential
85	value into command text, a script file, a log or a reply. Parse the values
86	inside the same command that sends the request, so they reach the HTTP client
87	without ever appearing in the command line or its output. One safe pattern
88	feeds the Basic pair to curl through its config on standard input:
89	
90	```sh
91	python3 -c 'import pathlib; e=dict(l.split("=",1) for l in pathlib.Path(".env").read_text().splitlines() if "=" in l and not l.lstrip().startswith("#")); print("user = \"%s:%s\"" % (e["XSOLLA_MERCHANT_ID"].strip(), e["XSOLLA_PROJECT_API_KEY"].strip()))' | curl -sS -K - "<route>"
92	```
93	
94	Resolve the three credential names as an all-or-nothing set:
95	
96	1. If all three process-environment values are present and non-empty, use that
97	   complete set.
98	2. Otherwise, if all three project-local `.env` values are present and
99	   non-empty, use that complete set.
100	3. Never combine process values with `.env` values. If neither source is
101	   complete, stop before network calls and tell the publisher to set
102	   `XSOLLA_MERCHANT_ID`, `XSOLLA_PROJECT_ID`, and
103	   `XSOLLA_PROJECT_API_KEY` in the project-local `.env` or process environment.
104	
105	For the Quest service selector, a process-environment value takes precedence
106	when present; otherwise read `XSOLLA_QP_ENV` from project-local `.env`. If the
107	selector is absent from both places, use `production`. Only `production` and
108	explicit `stage` are accepted. An explicitly present empty, whitespace-only, or
109	unsupported value is an error: stop before network calls and ask the publisher
110	to set it to `production` or `stage`. `XSOLLA_QP_ENV` selects Quest Platform
111	services (configuration, event ingestion, and execution read-back). It does not
112	select the Web3 catalog or minting lane, which remains production as documented
113	in Minting service. **STAGE DEMO ONLY:** the one exception is the
114	[stage demo gate](stage-demo.md#gate), which uses stage catalog and mint reads
115	for the demo scope. It is not a credential and merchant setup must preserve it.
116	Do not infer a target by probing hosts or by trying a credential against
117	multiple gateways.
118	
119	The versioned API contract maps `production` to
120	`https://quests-platform.xsolla.com` and `stage` to
121	`https://quests-stage.xsolla.com`.
122	
123	The catalog project is not a credential and must come from the resolved item,
124	never from the Quest Platform project by default.
125	
126	## The merchant id in the path
127	
128	When the contract uses merchant and project path parameters, both must come
129	from the same resolved credential set. Never take them from
130	the quest body, a read-back row, an earlier answer or a guess. A developer who
131	names another merchant or project needs the matching credential set.
132	
133	The server may stamp publisher and project fields from the route. Read them
134	back after creation and stop if they do not match the resolved scope.
135	
136	## Project-scoped routes
137	
138	Use the merchant/project-scoped Quest Platform route family in the
139	[versioned API contract](qp-api-contract.md):
140	
141	| Operation | Use |
142	|---|---|
143	| `GET /api/v2/merchants/{merchant_id}/projects/{project_id}` | verify scope and visibility |
144	| `GET /api/v2/merchants/{merchant_id}/projects/{project_id}/quests` | find an existing quest by paging |
145	| `POST /api/v2/merchants/{merchant_id}/projects/{project_id}/quests` | create with `status: inactive` for a draft |
146	| `GET` or `PUT /api/v2/merchants/{merchant_id}/projects/{project_id}/quests/{quest_id}` | read or replace one quest |
147	
148	Do not substitute an account-scoped, publisher-scoped or unscoped route from a
149	different authentication lane. A route absent from the versioned contract is
150	not called.
151	
152	## When a route is missing
153	
154	A 404 router miss means the method and path are not deployed at that location.
155	It is not proof of a bad credential or missing project:
156	
157	1. Stop and do not retry a guessed route.
158	2. For Quest Platform routes (configuration, event ingestion, execution
159	   read-back), compare with the versioned API contract. Consult published
160	   OpenAPI only when the selected target exposes it.
161	3. If the contract documents the same operation under another route, show the
162	   developer the proposed route and ask before calling it. For a write, show
163	   the request again.
164	4. If the operation is absent or not publisher-usable, report that it is
165	   unavailable and stop.
166	
167	## Reading a 401 or 404
168
